analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW — Capital preservation is the priority this cycle. The account has a 0% win rate across 13 trades, a -9.4% max drawdown, and a Sortino of -15.26. These are not noise; they are a loud signal to slow down, not accelerate.

AMP (CRITICAL THESIS BREAK): AMP is down 9.23% from entry and is NOT in this cycle's screened candidate list — meaning it very likely failed the 'no confirmed downtrend' filter. We previously exited AMP at -3.81% on a stop hit and re-entered the same deteriorating name. This is a repeated mistake against a declining trend. AMP should be exited at or near current price. Do not wait for a second stop to be hit at a larger loss. The pattern of re-entering a prior loser is exactly the behavior the strategy is designed to prevent.

FOXA (WATCH): Down 3.85% and also absent from the screened candidate list. Less urgent than AMP but the same concern applies — it may have failed trend or quality filters. If the stop triggers, accept it cleanly.

NVDA (HOLD, TIGHTEN STOP): Up 9.48% — the only clear winner. However, NVDA is now at its 52-week high (100% range position) and 8.9% above SMA50. Technically extended. Do not add here. Tighten the trailing stop toward $215-220 to protect gains on the ~$1,400 of open profit.

IT (THESIS WEAKENING): Revenue growth -0.6% and EPS revision -1.1% are concerning for a position entered on growth expectations. Essentially flat on P&L. Watch November 3rd earnings very closely; any top-line guidance cut is a thesis break and warrants exit.

ULTA (HOLD): Uptrend basing at 38% of 52w range. Thesis intact, earnings not until December. No action needed.

NEW TRADES — NONE: Market regime is unavailable, the win rate provides zero statistical evidence of a stock-picking edge, and we have active positions in names that may have failed the trend filter. With earnings season beginning in 2-3 weeks for most candidates (TEL Oct 28, HCA Oct 27, QCOM Nov 4, etc.), initiating new binary-event exposures adds risk the account cannot currently afford. TEL and QCOM present reasonable basing setups at fair valuations and merit watchlist priority for post-earnings entries, but neither clears the 'genuinely asymmetric AND capacity to size it properly' bar today. Holding ~39% cash while exiting AMP and monitoring FOXA is the disciplined, correct call. Cash is a position. Forcing a new BUY to feel productive is the enemy.
